The Date Game

Game StrategyLogicCounting

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)

Game: Move a calendar date forward to December 31. You and the computer take turns, and whoever gets there first wins.
How to play: Click the month or the day to move it forward, then press Move. Once you start with one, keep clicking that one until you press Move.
Month
Day

Look for the math

A calendar date looks like two ordinary numbers. But this game is an impartial game in disguise, and there is a short diagonal of losing dates hiding in the calendar.

A date is two numbers

Count months and days from zero: January is 0 and the 1st is 0, so December 31 is (11, 30). A move adds to one of the two numbers, and a real date must have its day inside that month — February 30 is not allowed. The player who reaches (11, 30) wins. This is an impartial game, the same family as Nim.

The losing diagonal

The twelve losing dates are Jan 20, Feb 21, Mar 22, Apr 23, May 24, Jun 25, Jul 26, Aug 27, Sep 28, Oct 29, Nov 30, Dec 31. In every one of them, day − month = 19, which is 30 − 11. From any other date, one move can put you back on that line: if the difference is too small, move the day up to month + 19; if it is too big, move the month up to day − 19. From the line, every move leaves it. So the line is exactly the set of losing positions, and the computer in the applet aims for it.

What the check found

The logic test searches the whole game tree of every valid date and finds exactly those twelve losing dates — the diagonal the cut-the-knot page describes. It repeats the search with a leap-year February and gets the same twelve, so the shorter months really do not shift the line. It also transcribes the applet's own computer move from the bytecode and compares the two on every playable date: they agree everywhere. One harmless quirk stays: the applet first checks whether day − month + 19 = 0, which can never happen, before using the real test. A second quirk is the date undo: change to a month with too few days and the whole turn is rolled back with an apology.

Start on January 20 and press Move without changing it. That is a losing date — can you see why every reply lets the computer take the diagonal?
